# 4ustre — design system

The personal brand of **Austė Vagoraitė**, an illustrator and graphic designer in Vilnius.
The work spans editorial illustration, book cover design, brand identity, wedding stationery,
illustrated products (pins, prints, shirts) and web design. Side projects — The Chips Critics
Club above all — are part of the brand, not a distraction from it.

**Personality:** naive but never sloppy. Drawn by a hand, not generated by a system. Tasteful,
modern, subtle, quietly strange. Restraint in layout so colour can be generous. The idea
arrives quietly; nothing shouts.

## Sources

- `uploads/4ustre.svg` — the creature logo, supplied by the user. Copied verbatim to `assets/logo.svg`
  (the only change: `.cls-1 { fill: currentColor }` so it can be inked or reversed). Never redrawn.
- `uploads/Design.pdf` — **referenced in the brief but not present on the filesystem.** Everything
  visual below therefore comes from the written brand brief, not from the PDF. If the PDF holds
  paintings, printed pieces or specimen pages, re-upload it and this system should be revised
  against it — particularly image treatment and any real photography.
- The written brand brief (colour values sampled from finished paintings, type rules, texture
  recipe, layout rules, voice) — the authority for this system.

No codebase, Figma file or deck was provided. No live site was read.

---

## Content fundamentals

Voice is **first person, singular**. Austė writes, not a studio. Plain short sentences, concrete
nouns, no marketing language. Where a page would normally sell, it invites instead.

- **Person:** "I drew the cover for Rasa's second novel." Never "we", never "the studio".
- **Casing:** sentence case everywhere. Uppercase is permitted **only** in small labels
  (12px, Medium 500, 0.16em tracking). No all-caps headlines, ever.
- **Specificity:** name the actual book, couple or crisp. "Elena & Jonas, letterpress, two passes"
  beats "wedding stationery project".
- **Humour:** dry, and at most one joke per page. "Restocked when I remember."
- **Invitation, not CTA:** "If you have an idea, I'd love to see where we could take it."
  Not "Let's create something amazing together".
- **Length:** a lead paragraph is one sentence. Body copy runs to 62ch and stops.
- **Emoji:** never. No exclamation marks in body copy. No underlines except a real hyperlink,
  and links are a hairline border-bottom rather than a text-decoration.

Yes / no, side by side:

> ✓ "Three greens, one crow, no time."
> ✗ "Delivering bespoke visual storytelling solutions."

Captions name the thing and its facts: subject, then publisher/photographer/year on a second line.

---

## Visual foundations

**Colour.** Ten values, all sampled from finished paintings; nothing invented. Paper `#F4EEE4`
and Ink `#241E1B` are the constant ground. Oyster Rose `#93495B` is the primary. A surface mixes
roughly **60% paper, 22% one section colour, 12% ink, 6% accent**. One section colour per piece,
never two — set `data-section="grass"` once, high in the tree, and everything below inherits
`--surface-field` / `--text-on-field`. Marigold and Poppy stay small: a rule, a dot, one word.

**Type.** Instrument Serif for display and titles — regular and italic only, **never bolded**,
tight leading, −0.02em tracking above 60px. Hanken Grotesk for body, captions and labels: Light
300 for long text, Medium 500 for labels. Left-aligned as a rule. No letter-spaced body copy.
Both families are loaded from Google Fonts (see *Font substitution* below).

**Backgrounds.** Cream paper, edge to edge, or one flat colour field. No photography as
background, no repeating patterns, no gradients — ever. Full-bleed images are used deliberately
(two-thirds of a surface with a caption beneath), not decoratively.

**Texture.** Flat colour is always slightly disturbed by a soft paper grain: an SVG fractal noise
tile, `mix-blend-mode: multiply`, **12% over paper, 18% over a colour field, 20% ceiling on the
darkest fields**. Use the `.grain` class or the `--grain-url` token. In print: uncoated cream
stock, never gloss.

**Shadows, glows, gradients.** None. `--shadow-none` exists so the answer is written down. Depth
comes from colour blocks and hairlines, not from lighting.

**Borders and radii.** Hairline `1px` at `--ink-14`, rules at `--ink-38`. Radii are effectively
zero — `--radius-none` is the default and the image edge is the card edge. Two exceptions: the
**pill** (`999px`) on buttons and tags, and the **circle** crop for images and title fields.

**Cards.** No border, no shadow, no rounding, no background. A card is an image, a small
uppercase label, and a serif title, stacked with 16px gaps. Nothing floats.

**Animation.** Sparing and short. `--motion-base: 240ms` on
`cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1)`; colour and opacity only. Nothing moves, scales, bounces or
parallaxes — the page is a printed sheet that happens to respond.

**Hover.** Colour change, not movement: a project title takes the section colour; a link's
hairline takes the accent; a primary button darkens from Oyster Rose to Ink; a reversed button on
a field fills with cream. **Press:** no shrink — hold the hover colour. **Disabled:** 38% opacity.
**Focus:** a 1px ink outline; never a glow.

**Transparency and blur.** Transparency only as ink or paper tints (`--ink-60`, `--paper-24`) for
hairlines and muted text. **Blur is never used** — no frosted panels, no protection gradients.
If text needs to sit on colour, it sits on a flat field or in a cream circle.

**Imagery.** Warm, painted, matte: gouache and pastel on rough paper, cream-biased, with grain.
Never cool, never glossy, never black and white, never a stock photograph. Where artwork is not
yet available, `ImageFrame` renders a grained flat section colour naming the intended subject —
an honest hole, not a fake illustration.

**Layout.** 12 columns, 32px gutters, wide margins (96px, 160px on generous pages), one idea per
surface. Three recurring arrangements, each available as a class in `tokens/layout.css` and as a
component:
1. Text left with the image bleeding off the right edge (`.arr-text-bleed`, `ImageFrame bleed="right"`).
2. A circle holding an image or a title on a flat colour field (`.arr-circle`, `ColorField circle`).
3. A full-bleed image over two thirds with a caption beneath (`.arr-bleed-cap`).

Nothing is fixed or sticky; the header scrolls away like a page turning. If in doubt, remove
something.

---

## Iconography

**There is no icon set in this brand, and none has been invented.** The supplied materials contain
exactly one drawn asset — the creature logo. Interfaces are carried by type, colour and the logo.

- **Navigation and actions** use words, not glyphs: "All work", "Read the notes", "Send it".
- Where a directional cue is genuinely needed, use the typographic characters already in the
  fonts: `→`, `←`, `·`. Nothing else.
- **No icon font, no SVG sprite, no Lucide/Heroicons/Feather substitution.** Adding a third-party
  stroke set would contradict the hand-drawn premise, so it is deliberately absent. If the brand
  ever needs icons (a shop cart, a social row), they should be **drawn by Austė** in the same ink
  as the creature and added to `assets/` — not linked from a CDN.
- **Emoji: never.**
- The logo doubles as the only "icon": at 32–40px it is a corner stamp signing a page.

### Logo rules

Solid ink on cream, reversed cream on a colour field, stacked above the wordmark, or small as a
corner stamp. Clear space equals the height of the creature's ear (`0.18 × size`). Minimum **32px
digital, 12mm print**. Never redrawn, smoothed, outlined, rotated, stretched or shadowed, and
never in a colour outside the palette. See `guidelines/brand-*.html`.

---

## Font substitution — needs your input

No font binaries were supplied. Instrument Serif and Hanken Grotesk are both available on Google
Fonts and are loaded from there in `tokens/fonts.css` (Instrument Serif 400 + italic; Hanken
Grotesk 300 / 400 / 500) — so the families are correct, but they are CDN-hosted rather than
self-hosted, and the design system reports **0 `@font-face` rules**. **If you have licensed
`.woff2` files, send them and I'll self-host them with real `@font-face` rules.**

## Intentional additions

Nothing in the brief enumerated a component inventory, so a small set was authored to the brand's
actual needs. Two are additions worth naming:

- **`ColorField`** — encodes "one section colour per piece" and the circle arrangement as a single
  surface, so the rule is enforced by the component rather than remembered.
- **`Label`** — exists so uppercase tracking is only ever reachable through a component that is
  never used for headlines.

## Index

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `styles.css` | The one file consumers link. `@import`s only. |
| `tokens/colors.css` | Palette, paper/ink tints, semantic aliases, the nine `data-section` scopes |
| `tokens/typography.css` | Families, weights, display + text scale, `--type-*` shorthands, measures |
| `tokens/spacing.css` | 8px scale, semantic gaps, radii, `--shadow-none` |
| `tokens/texture.css` | The grain recipe (`--grain-url`, opacities, `.grain`) |
| `tokens/layout.css` | Grid, margins, motion, and the three arrangement classes |
| `tokens/base.css` | Element defaults: paper, ink, serif headings, link styling |
| `tokens/fonts.css` | Webfont loading (Google Fonts) |
| `assets/logo.svg` | The creature mark, verbatim |
| `thumbnail.html` | Homepage tile |

**Components** (`window.Ds4ustreDesignSystem_43cae6`)

| Component | Directory |
| --- | --- |
| `Logo` | `components/brand/` — mark, lockup, stamp; ink or reversed |
| `Button` | `components/core/` — primary, secondary, ghost, onField; 3 sizes |
| `Label` | `components/core/` — the only uppercase |
| `Tag` | `components/core/` — outline, quiet, field, accent |
| `Caption` | `components/media/` — subject + credit |
| `ImageFrame` | `components/media/` — rect, circle crop, bleed; always grained |
| `ProjectCard` | `components/cards/` — work index card |
| `ColorField` | `components/layout/` — section colour surface, optional circle |

Each directory holds `<Name>.jsx`, `<Name>.d.ts`, `<Name>.prompt.md` and a `@dsCard` HTML.

**Guidelines cards** — `guidelines/*.html`, grouped as Colors, Type, Texture, Spacing, Layout, Brand.

**UI kit** — `ui_kits/website/` — 4ustre.lt: home, work index, project, about + contact, shop.

**SKILL.md** — makes this folder usable as an Agent Skill in Claude Code.
